title: haruspex.ir.json
description: An IR file of version 0.32, 0.31, 0.30, 0.29, 0.28, 0.27, 0.26, 0.25, 0.24 or 0.23: the shapes haruspex inferred for a set of database objects, of one database or (0.24) combining two, (0.25) where each field's value came from, (0.26) the table types its parameters take, (0.27) binary values, (0.28) the columns the config file declares to hold JSON of a schema, (0.29) what makes a reason so, in words, and a minimum length in code points, (0.30) the build that wrote it, (0.31) the packages the config file declared builds, and (0.32) the folders of a source read from several. The format is described in src/Haruspex.Ir/README.md.

irVersion.description: The IR's version, which a reader checks before anything else, the oldest that says all the document says: 0.32 for a document whose source was read from several folders (source.paths, or its baseline's), else 0.31 for one that records packages declared builds (source.builds, or its baseline's), else 0.30 for one that names the build that wrote it (source.writtenBy), else 0.29 for one in which a reason says what makes it so or a minimum length is in code points (a detail or a minimum's unit, which this schema can't require), else 0.28 for one that declares a column's JSON (columns, or what only a declaration gives: any JSON, a fact from a declaration or an open object, which this schema can't require), else 0.27 for one that holds a binary value (a scalar of kind bytes, which this schema can't require), else 0.26 for one that defines a table type, else 0.25 for one that says where a field's value came from, else 0.24 for one combining two databases, else 0.23.

source.description: Where the shapes were inferred from.

dialect.description: The SQL dialect, such as tsql.

path.description: Where the source was read from, as the config file names it: relative to its folder, /-separated (0.25). Left out when not known, and for a source read from several folders.

paths.description: For a source read from several folders of scripts as one database, the folders, each by its name as found on disk relative to the config file's folder, /-separated, as the locations name it, sorted (0.32). Every location into the source's scripts is then relative to the config file's folder, and so begins with the folder listed, rather than relative to one folder read. Left out for a source read from one folder, a project or a package, which path names.

package.description: The file name of the package the source was read from, such as a DACPAC. Left out for a source that is not a package.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the package's bytes. Given exactly when package is.

references.description: The packages the package refers to, found or not, sorted by name and then database. Left out when there are none.

builds.description: The packages the config file declared builds, of those the source read: its package and the references found, by the names they give them, sorted (0.31). Their primary keys and unique constraints are claimed on the user's word. Left out when none is declared.

items.description: A package's file name, as package or a reference names it.

session.description: The options the callers' sessions are declared to set, by the dialect's name for each: true for on, false for off. Left out when none is declared.

files.description: The SHA-256 of each script file the document's locations point into, by its path as a location writes it (relative to the folder read, or to the config file's folder when paths is given), of its text with LF line endings in UTF-8 (0.25). Left out when there are none.

baseline.description: For a document combining two databases (0.24), where the other, the baseline, was read from. Always given when irVersion is 0.24, never when it is 0.23.

dialect.description: The SQL dialect, such as tsql.

path.description: Where the source was read from, as the config file names it: relative to its folder, /-separated (0.25). Left out when not known, and for a source read from several folders.

paths.description: For a source read from several folders of scripts as one database, the folders, each by its name as found on disk relative to the config file's folder, /-separated, as the locations name it, sorted (0.32). Every location into the source's scripts is then relative to the config file's folder, and so begins with the folder listed, rather than relative to one folder read. Left out for a source read from one folder, a project or a package, which path names.

package.description: The file name of the package the source was read from, such as a DACPAC. Left out for a source that is not a package.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the package's bytes. Given exactly when package is.

references.description: The packages the package refers to, found or not, sorted by name and then database. Left out when there are none.

builds.description: The packages the config file declared builds, of those the source read: its package and the references found, by the names they give them, sorted (0.31). Their primary keys and unique constraints are claimed on the user's word. Left out when none is declared.

items.description: A package's file name, as package or a reference names it.

session.description: The options the callers' sessions are declared to set, by the dialect's name for each: true for on, false for off. Left out when none is declared.

files.description: The SHA-256 of each script file the document's locations point into, by its path as a location writes it (relative to the folder read, or to the config file's folder when paths is given), of its text with LF line endings in UTF-8 (0.25). Left out when there are none.

types.description: The named object types, by name.

tableTypes.description: The table types the parameters take, by the key a parameter's tableType names (0.26). Always given when irVersion is 0.26, never before it, and when it is 0.27 exactly when a parameter takes a table type.

columns.description: The columns the config file declares to hold JSON of a schema, sorted by column (0.28). Never given before 0.28.

folds.description: The folds the canonical value sets name, by name: how a collation compares a column's strings (0.20).

build.description: The build of the tool that wrote the source's claims (0.30). Always given for a document's own source when irVersion is 0.30 or later, never before it; a baseline's is left out when not known.

version.description: The tool's version, as it says it, without the commit.

commit.description: The whole commit the build was made from; left out when the build didn't know it.

packageReference.description: A package the source's package refers to.

package.description: Its file name, as the referring package names it.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the package read for it; left out when none was found.

database.description: Left out for the same database; otherwise the other database, by name or SQLCMD variable, as the reference names it.

object.description: A typed object: a procedure of the database, or a query file of the application.

id.description: Its identity: a procedure's name in the database, or a query file's path relative to its config file's folder.

name.description: The name settled for generated code.

at.description: Where it is defined, as path:line:column.

text.description: What a query runs, as one batch, with LF line endings; only a query has it, and a query always does.

returnsCode.description: Whether a call may end with a return code other than 0.

results.description: Its result sets in order, or null when they cannot be listed; named all or none.

name.description: Its name as declared, with its sigil.

tableType.description: For a table-valued parameter (0.26), the key of its type's definition in tableTypes; left out for any other.

hasDefault.description: Whether the caller may omit it.

output.description: Whether it is an output parameter.

name.description: The set's name, a key of the object its function returns; left out when the object's sets are unnamed, and given for all of them or none.

mayBeAbsent.description: Whether the result can arrive with no value at all.

rows.description: What a rowset's type is: one statement's rows, or a union of several statements' when paths differ.

statementRows.description: One statement's rows: an array of a named object type or of an unknown, an unknown, or what the config file declared them to be.

declaredType.description: A type the config file declared, or arrays of one.

recursive.description: Whether the type refers to itself; left out when it doesn't.

nameDeclared.description: Whether the config file gave the type its name; left out when the naming rules did.

open.description: Whether its values may hold keys it doesn't list, of any value (0.28): JSON a column is declared to hold; left out when they hold only its fields' keys.

identity.description: Where a type comes from: the database object it belongs to, keyed by the object's kind, and the path to it there.

procedure.description: The procedure the type belongs to.

function.description: The function the type belongs to.

query.description: The query the type belongs to.

tableType.description: The tableType the type belongs to.

path.description: The path to the type, in the IR's path syntax.

tableType.description: A table type's definition (0.26): what a table-valued parameter of it takes.

schema.description: The schema it is defined in.

at.description: Where it is defined, as path:line:column.

columns.description: Its columns in the order declared, which is the order a client sends them in.

checks.description: Its CHECK constraints' conditions, each as written, on one line.

tableColumn.description: A column of a table type.

sql.description: Its type as the database spells it; left out only for a computed column.

nullable.description: Whether a row may hold NULL in it.

collation.description: The collation its strings compare under, when known; left out otherwise.

tableKey.description: A key of a table type: columns whose values no two rows may share.

ignoresDuplicates.description: Whether a row whose key another has is dropped without an error; left out when false.

field.description: A field of an object type.

nullable.description: Whether the value can be null.

sides.description: In a document combining two databases (0.25), the field as each gave it; a side is left out where that database doesn't return the key.

from.description: The table columns a value is read from, in the order the SQL first reads them (0.25). Left out when it reads none directly.

sourceColumn.description: A table column a value is read from (0.25).

sql.description: The column's type as a scalar's sql is written; left out when it is not a scalar the IR types.

at.description: Where the column is declared, as path:line:column.

side.description: A field as one of the two combined databases gives it (0.25).

nullable.description: Whether that database's value can be null.

sql.description: The value's SQL type there, when it is a scalar.

reasons.description: Why a value can be null, or a result absent: at least one reason.

reason.description: One reason a value can be null.

at.description: What the rule applies to: a column or a source location.

detail.description: What makes it so, in words, when there is more to say than the rule (0.29): for a value read from JSON at a path, the steps that may find nothing or null.

type.description: A type node: a reference to a named type, or a kind.

ref.description: A reference to a named object type.

scalar.description: A scalar with its logical kind, the SQL type it came from, and its facets.

sql.description: The source's own type, as written.

length.description: A string's length: a maximum (maxLength) or a fixed length (length).

minLength.description: A string's minimum length, in UTF-16 code units, or (0.29) in code points when its unit says so.

unit.description: What value counts when not UTF-16 code units (0.29).

bound.description: A bound on a number: exact decimal text written as a JSON number, in plain form (no exponent), which a reader must not round. JSON Schema can't check a number's form; the reader refuses any other.

inclusive.description: Whether the bound itself is allowed.

values.description: A set the value is drawn from.

items.description: The values: strings, or numbers in plain decimal form (no exponent), which JSON Schema can't check and the reader does.

fold.description: The name of the fold in folds that gives a value's canonical form: present exactly when the match is canonical.

How a collation compares a column's strings. A string's canonical form drops each character of ignored, puts a class's name in place of each character of that class, keeps every other character, and then drops trailing spaces (U+0020), in that order.

ignored.description: The characters ignored, in ordinal order.

classes.description: The characters of each class, in ordinal order, by the class's name, which is what they become.

factSource.description: Where a fact came from: one property, named for the kind of source, whose value is the type's or constraint's name or a location.

type.description: The type the fact came from.

check.description: The check the fact came from.

engine.description: The engine the fact came from.

expression.description: The expression the fact came from.

declared.description: The declared the fact came from.

itemsNullable.description: Whether an item can be null; left out when none can.

tuple.description: An array of a fixed length whose every position has its own type.

nullable.description: Whether the element can be null.

record.description: An object whose keys are data, every value of one type.

valuesNullable.description: Whether a value can be null.

union.description: A value that has one of several types.

jsonText.description: A string that holds JSON, with what it parses to when that is known.

anyJson.description: Any JSON value (0.28): an object, an array, a string, a number, a boolean or null, of any content.

objectOrArray.description: Whether it is only ever an object or an array; left out when it may be any JSON value.

columnDeclaration.description: A column the config file declares to hold JSON of a schema (0.28).

schema.description: The schema file, relative to the folder of the config file, /-separated.

pointer.description: The JSON Pointer to the schema used inside the file, when not the whole file.

files.description: The SHA-256 of every schema file the declaration read, by its path, written as schema is.

import.description: A schema the application already has, which the config file declared.

from.description: The module it is exported by.

unknownType.description: A value whose type is not known.

unknown.description: Something that could not be typed.

object.description: The id of the object it belongs to.

path.description: Where in the object, in the IR's path syntax.

at.description: The source location of the construct.

override.description: A claim the config file made rather than inference.

object.description: The id of the object it applies to.

path.description: Where in the object, in the IR's path syntax.

via.description: What the claim rests on, when not the object's own declaration: the procedure whose declared results it includes, or (0.28) the declared column it reads.

why.description: The reason given in the config file.
